jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
Vice President of Finance – Canada

Location: Calgary, AB

Company: Hero Canada Foods Inc.

About Hero Canada Foods

Hero Canada Foods is a leading branded food company and part of the international Hero Group, headquartered in Switzerland. In Canada, Hero is known for its successful portfolio of brands including Baby Gourmet, Simply Gourmet, and Goodies. Hero Canada combines local entrepreneurial agility with the scale, expertise, and long-term perspective of an international food group and is investing in systems, processes, commercial capabilities, and organizational maturity to support profitable growth.

Role Summary

Hero Canada Foods is seeking a VP of Finance to lead all finance activities in Canada and serve as a key member of the leadership team. Reporting to the General Manager and partnering closely with Hero Group Finance, the VP Finance provides strategic financial leadership while maintaining a strong connection to the commercial and operational drivers of the business.

The VP Finance supports the General Manager in shaping strategy, setting priorities, evaluating opportunities, and navigating day-to-day operational decisions. The role provides clear financial guidance and constructive challenges while remaining close enough to the work to turn insight into action quickly.

The VP Finance will actively partner with the Commercial Finance Manager on pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, forecasting, and business case development, providing both strategic guidance and direct analytical support as needed. At the same time, they will lead a transactional accounting team consisting of a Senior Accountant, an Accounts Payable Accountant, and an Accounts Receivable Accountant, ensuring accurate reporting, disciplined controls, and reliable execution.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Partner to the General Manager

Act as the General Manager’s trusted finance adviser on business strategy, growth priorities, organizational choices, investments, risks, and operational trade-offs.
Provide practical, fact-based guidance on day-to-day business matters, combining strategic perspective with an understanding of operational detail.
Translate financial and commercial information into clear choices, recommendations, scenarios, and actions for the General Manager and leadership team.
Constructively challenge assumptions and help align local decisions with Hero Canada’s objectives and Hero Group expectations.
Support the development and execution of the Canadian strategy, including profitable growth, margin improvement, cash generation, and operating profit protection.

2. Hands-on Commercial Finance Leadership

Lead and actively support the Commercial Finance Manager, providing coaching, prioritization, technical guidance, and direct practical assistance.
Lead financial analysis related to pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, promotions, and margin optimization, personally reviewing and supporting detailed financial models where appropriate.
Personally review, adjust, and, where required, build or manipulate detailed Excel-based pricing and commercial models rather than operating only at review level.
Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve decision quality and visibility of margins, cost drivers, pricing impacts, working capital, and profitability.
Ensure financial analysis is commercially relevant, technically sound, timely, and converted into clear recommendations.

3. Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budgeting process, rolling forecasts, performance reviews, and longer-term financial projections.
Connect commercial assumptions, supply chain realities, operating costs, and strategic initiatives into an integrated financial plan.
Monitor business performance, identify emerging gaps and opportunities, and establish corrective measures with accountable business owners.
Prepare clear reporting and decision materials for the General Manager, Canadian leadership team, Board, and Hero Group stakeholders.
Use scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to support decisions under uncertainty.

4. Accounting, Reporting & Transactional Finance Leadership

Lead the Senior Accountant, Accounts Payable Accountant, and Accounts Receivable Accountant, establishing clear ownership, priorities, service standards, and controls.
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and year-end close and ensure timely, accurate, and transparent reporting to local management and Hero Group.
Ensure accurate accounting in accordance with applicable accounting standards and Hero Group reporting requirements.
Maintain a strong internal-control environment across order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, payroll, inventory, and treasury processes.
Remain sufficiently close to transactional workflows to resolve issues, remove bottlenecks, improve quality, and provide hands-on support during peak periods or complex matters.
Drive pragmatic process improvements, automation, clear documentation, and stronger use of systems and data.

5. Cash Flow, Working Capital & Risk Management

Own cash flow planning, liquidity, and working capital performance, with focused management of receivables, payables, inventory, and operating commitments.
Identify and manage financial and operational exposures, including insurance, contracts, customer and supplier risk, and foreign exchange where relevant.
Support capital allocation, funding, and investment decisions with disciplined financial analysis and recommendations.
Serve as the primary financial steward of the Canadian business, ensuring decisions support sustainable value creation and alignment with Hero Group objectives.

6. Compliance, Tax & Governance

Ensure compliance with national, provincial, local, and Hero Group financial requirements.
Coordinate external audit, tax, payroll, benefits, legal, insurance, and advisory partners as required.
Oversee statutory filings, tax compliance, transfer pricing support, corporate governance requirements, and Group reporting obligations.
Ensure appropriate documentation, approval authorities, and segregation-of-duties or compensating controls are maintained.

7. Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build one connected finance team across commercial finance and accounting, balancing business partnership with reliable transaction processing and control.
Build finance talent and organizational capability through coaching, development planning, succession management, and cross-functional business exposure.
Develop the Commercial Finance Manager as a strong business partner while remaining available for detailed technical and modelling support.
Create a working culture that values accuracy, pace, ownership, practical problem-solving, continuous improvement, and constructive challenge.
Provide clear goals, coaching, feedback, succession planning, and development opportunities.

Team Structure

Reports to: General Manager, Hero Canada
Functional connection: Hero Group Finance
Direct leadership over: Commercial Finance Manager; Senior Accountant; Accounts Payable Accountant; Accounts Receivable Accountant

Required Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including meaningful senior finance leadership responsibility.
Experience serving as a CFO, VP Finance, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leader within a growth-oriented, lean operating environment.
Strong commercial finance experience with demonstrated depth in pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.
Advanced Excel capability and willingness to work directly in detailed models and analyses.
Strong technical foundation in financial reporting, accounting, internal controls, cash flow, working capital, audit, tax, and compliance.
Experience leading both commercially oriented finance professionals and transactional accounting teams.
Experience in an international or cross-border business environment; CPG, food, manufacturing, distribution, or branded consumer products experience preferred.
Experience leading finance process improvements, ERP implementations, reporting enhancements, and finance transformation initiatives.

Key Competencies

Strategic and commercial mindset
Hands-on analytical and problem-solving capability
Influence and stakeholder management
Financial stewardship and risk management
Leadership and talent development
Continuous improvement orientation
Executive communication and presentation skills
High integrity and sound judgment
Financial modelling, analytical, and technical accounting capability

jobs.title: Director, Newcomer Channel Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
Job Description

What’s the Opportunity?

Newcomers are critical client segment for RBC, with distinct needs across their journey - from preparing to move to Canada, to establishing their financial lives upon arrival, to building deeper financial relationships as they settle and grow.

As Director, Newcomer Channel Strategy & Operations
, you will lead the strategy and evolution of the channels, capabilities and partnership operations required to deliver a differentiated newcomer banking proposition. You will own the "how" behind our newcomer strategy: translating our ambition into intuitive client journeys, scalable capabilities, effective frontline experiences and an ecosystem of services that helps newcomers establish their lives in Canada.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You will work across Everyday Banking & Client Growth, Product, Digital, Enablement, Advice Centre, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Marketing, and external partners to identify friction, establish priorities, and mobilize the organization around a multi-year newcomer journey.

What You'll Do

Own the End-To-End Newcomer Onboarding Experience

Develop and continuously evolve the target experience for newcomers across key moments in their journey - from pre-arrival through onboarding, settlement, and early relationship growth
Map and assess end-to-end newcomer journeys across digital, assisted, and non-traditional channels
Identify the highest impact experience gaps, friction points, and capability opportunities
Define the target state newcomer experience and work cross-functionally to define it into a prioritized roadmap
Establish clear experience principles and standards that can be applied across products and channels
Partner with Product and Journey teams to ensure newcomer needs are incorporated into broader enterprise roadmaps rather than addressed solely through segment-specific initiatives

Own the Pre-Arrival Account Open Capability

Own and continuously evolve the end-to-end pre-arrival account open capability, ensuring a seamless accessible and differentiated experience for newcomers establishing their relationship before coming to Canada
Define the strategic direction and prioritized roadmap for pre-arrival account opening, identifying opportunities to enhance functionality, simplify the client experience and expand acquisition opportunities
Identify and address capability gaps, client friction points, and operational inefficiencies across the pre-arrival account opening journey, from application and identity verification through account activation and funding
Partner with Digital, Product, Technology, Business Development, Operations and Risk teams to deliver capability enhancements that balance client experience, business growth, operational scalability and regulatory requirements
Identify opportunities to expand the reach and effectiveness of pre-arrival account opening across priority newcomer markets, acquisition channels and strategic partnerships

Enable Newcomer Onboarding, Policy & Process

Lead the efforts to remove unnecessary complexity from how newcomers establish a banking relationship while ensuring appropriate risk and regulatory requirements are maintained
Identify policies or processes creating disproportionate friction for newcomers
Clarify documentation, identification, residency and eligibility requirements
Challenge legacy processes and distinguish true regulatory requirements from internal practices
Design scalable solutions that balance client experience, growth, operational simplicity and risk
Improve consistency in how newcomer policies are understood and executed across channels Own the Newcomer Channel Strategy
Define how newcomer clients should be served across digital, branch, AC, and non-traditional channels (i.e. referral partnerships), including the role each channel plays throughout the journey.
Identify capabilities required to increase digital self-service while preserving high-value human advice
Partner with digital and journey teams to influence enterprise capability roadmaps
Work with distribution leaders to understand frontline friction and execution gaps
Ensure new capabilities and propositions can be delivered consistently across channels

Develop the Beyond Banking Newcomer Ecosystem

Help evolve the newcomer value proposition beyond traditional banking products by identifying and activating services and partnerships that solve meaningful settlement needs (i.e. housing readiness, employment/career support, immigration and settlement services, etc.)

Deliver Newcomer Advisor Enablement

Ensure frontline employees have the knowledge, tools, and capabilities to deliver a differentiated newcomer experience by working in partnership with enablement and the Advice Centre (Newcomer COE):

Define the ideal newcomer advisor experience
Simplify complex policies and product information
Develop tools and frameworks that support needs-based advice
Improve frontline awareness of newcomer beyond banking offers and resources
Create feedback loops between NCOE and National Office Newcomer Client Segment team to remain aware of key challenges, issues, or escalations.

What do you need to succeed?

Must-have

8+ years of experience in strategy, client experience, digital transformation, product management, operations or financial services.
Proven experience leading complex enterprise initiatives across highly matrixed organizations.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategic priorities into scalable business capabilities and operational outcomes.
Strong understanding of client journey design, digital enablement and experience transformation.
Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills across senior leadership teams.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
Strong executive communication skills with the ability to simplify complex topics and influence strategic decisions.
University degree or equivalent experience.

Nice-to-have

Experience in client onboarding, customer experience, digital transformation or capability strategy.
Experience working with partner ecosystems or enterprise implementations.
Experience in retail banking, payments or financial services.
MBA or equivalent graduate degree.
Experience serving newcomer or internationally mobile client segments.

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
Opportunities to do challenging work

jobs.title: Director, Technology Product Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Join our U.S. Technology Strategy and Architecture team as Director, Technology Product Strategy, where you will play a key role in supporting the development and execution of technology strategy across RBC’s U.S. organization.

Working closely with U.S. Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership, business lines, technology teams, and enterprise architecture, you will help shape the strategic direction of the U.S. technology organization. You will analyze the technology landscape, support strategic planning and investment decisions, and work across business and technology teams to advance key priorities.

This role provides broad exposure across the U.S. technology organization and an opportunity to work on some of its most important strategic questions. You will combine structured problem solving, technology knowledge, stakeholder management, and executive communication to support senior leaders in making informed technology decisions and advancing the U.S. technology agenda.

What will you do?

Support target-state strategy development: Partner with Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership to develop and maintain forward-looking U.S. technology strategy and, where required, business-line technology strategies. Gather inputs, assess strategic alternatives, and translate direction into clear target-state objectives, principles, KPIs, and priorities.
Maintain a view of the technology estate: Develop and maintain a comprehensive view of the U.S. technology landscape, bringing together information on applications, platforms, infrastructure, capabilities, dependencies, and investments to support strategic planning and decision-making.
Conduct strategic analyses: Perform structured, point-in-time analyses of technology opportunities, challenges, and strategic questions. Synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, evaluate alternatives, and develop recommendations for leadership consideration.
Support strategic alignment: Work with business and technology stakeholders to assess the alignment of major initiatives, programs, and investments with U.S. technology strategy and enterprise priorities. Identify potential gaps or areas of misalignment and support development of appropriate actions.
Support roadmap and funding decisions: Develop analyses and decision materials that help leadership evaluate technology roadmaps, investment priorities, dependencies, trade-offs, and funding requirements.
Support architecture governance and control: Partner with Enterprise Architecture and technology teams to facilitate architecture governance activities, track strategic and architectural decisions, identify areas requiring escalation, and support alignment with established architecture principles and target states.
Coordinate strategic planning activities: Support recurring strategy, roadmap, portfolio, and governance processes across the U.S. technology organization, ensuring stakeholders have the information and analysis required to make timely decisions.
Develop executive-level materials: Translate complex technology topics into concise presentations, recommendations, business cases, and decision materials for senior technology and business leadership.
Monitor strategic progress: Develop and maintain KPIs, KRIs, and other measures that provide visibility into progress against technology strategies, roadmaps, strategic initiatives, and architectural objectives.
Build organizational capability: Support the development and adoption of frameworks, methodologies, tools, templates, and ways of working that strengthen technology strategy and architecture capabilities across the U.S. organization.
Facilitate cross-functional collaboration: Coordinate across business lines, technology teams, architecture, finance, risk, and other stakeholders to gather inputs, resolve issues, and support decisions on cross-cutting technology priorities.
Identify emerging issues and opportunities: Analyze trends across the technology estate and external technology landscape to identify potential capability gaps, duplication, architectural constraints, emerging technologies, and opportunities for strategic improvement.

What do you need to succeed?

Must have:

Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience in technology, business, engineering, finance, or a related field.
10+ years of experience across technology strategy, enterprise architecture, technology transformation, management consulting, technology program management, or related disciplines.
Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience structuring ambiguous problems and developing fact-based recommendations.
Ability to understand complex technology environments and connect technology considerations to broader business and strategic objectives.
Experience supporting technology strategies, roadmaps, business cases, investment decisions, operating models, or transformation initiatives.
Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear presentations and decision materials.
Strong stakeholder management skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively across business and technology organizations.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a complex, matrixed environment.
Strong understanding of technology and/or the financial services industry.
Experience using current AI tooling to support research, automate repetitive tasks, analyze large data sets, etc.

Nice to have:

Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
Experience in a matrix environment, such as a large, publicly traded corporation.

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable.
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities.
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact.
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.
A world-class training program in financial services.

jobs.title: Director of Portfolio Finance
jobs.description:
The opportunity

We are building a centralized finance function for our portfolio, and we are looking for the person to lead it. You will give Rhyno greater control over cash, faster and more reliable reporting, and the financial credibility to work with lenders and financing partners from a position of strength.
This role suits someone who is comfortable deep in the numbers and equally comfortable stepping back to tell the partners clearly what they see: where each business stands, what healthy looks like, and how far there is to go.

What you will do

1. Treasury and liquidity

Own rolling 13-week cash flow forecasts across all six companies, refreshed weekly with variance analysis against actuals.
Build the 12 to 24 month liquidity outlook that feeds budgets and planning.
Manage AP prioritization and supplier payment plans and monitor bank accounts and cash daily.
Track available credit and covenant headroom under base and downside cases and flag liquidity risks early.
Manage banking relationships, account structures and intercompany funding across the portfolio.

2. Financial reporting
Accelerate month-end and annual financial reporting across the portfolio.
Improve consolidation, and set a common reporting template, chart of accounts mapping and reporting calendar for every company.
Produce a weekly liquidity view and a monthly reporting package for Rhyno leadership.
Set the cadence and content of financial reporting for board meetings.
Coordinate year-end audits with external auditors.

3. Budgeting and forecasting
Lead the annual budget for each company and for the consolidated portfolio.
Run rolling forecasts and monthly variance analysis and hold company leaders accountable to plan.
Benchmark each company's P&L against a healthy business in its space and set clear targets for where it should be.

4. Operational advisory
Identify cash flow inefficiencies across receivables, payables and inventory, and set working capital targets with each company.
Tie project billing (schedules of billings, progress draws and holdbacks) to cash so invoicing moves on time.
Advise leadership on operational resizing and cost reductions.
Find quick wins across the portfolio in financial systems, operations and management practices.
Strengthen financial controls, including payment approvals, signing authority and fraud prevention.
Step in hands-on when a company is under cash pressure, and coach company finance teams on cash discipline.

5. Lender readiness
Produce accurate, consistent, lender-ready reporting that shows forecasting reliability, financial control and management accountability.
Prepare covenant calculations, borrowing base certificates and lender reporting.
Lead responses to lender and auditor requests.
Support credit renewals, amendments and financing discussions alongside Rhyno leadership.

How success is measured
Weekly cash forecast accuracy within agreed tolerance across the portfolio.
Faster, more reliable month-end and year-end reporting.
Cash released through working capital improvement against target.
No covenant breaches or liquidity surprises.
On-time, credible reporting to the board and lenders.
Continuous improvement in systems and processes across every portfolio finance department, with each company's finance lead supported in driving their own improvements.

What you bring
CPA with 5 to 10+ years of relevant experience.
Background in PE-backed manufacturing, multi-entity finance or corporate restructuring.
Hands-on experience with refinancing, liquidity management and financial reporting.
Strong operational understanding, beyond accounting or FP&A alone.
Experience as a Finance Director, Divisional CFO or Senior Finance Manager in a $50M to $300M manufacturing business, or in a restructuring or advisory practice.
Ability to shift priorities quickly and move with speed, without compromising accuracy or momentum.
Autonomy and confidence to make decisions with the information available and bring strong, clear recommendations to the partners and board.
An owner’s approach to results, with hands-on accountability from building the model to presenting the findings.
A continuous improvement approach, with the curiosity to test the numbers, dig into root causes and bring structure where there isn’t any.
Ability to build trust with company leaders and finance teams through clear, direct communication, high integrity and composure under pressure.

Compensation
Base salary of $160,000 to $190,000, plus performance bonus and benefits.
How to apply
Please send your resume to Michelle McDonald, Head of Talent, Rhyno Equity Group.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Rhyno Equity Group is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to a hiring process free from discrimination, in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code.

Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process, in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Please let us know if you require an accommodation.

All applicants who are interviewed will be informed of the status of their application within 45 days of their final interview.
